details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:16997-17012 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `needs_human_park_project` skips parking whenever `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_ENABLED` is true, including terminal projects the unblock judge will not process.
  WHY: Those projects remain in terminal states without a digest entry; the reviewers rated this BLOCKER and MAJOR, respectively.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:120-128, 470-489 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `needs_human_park` adds `ai:needs-human` before the digest update succeeds, and an already-present label can make the label-add fail.
  WHY: A failed digest operation after the label is added leaves the item labeled with its trusted close marker but absent from the digest, so later scans skip it; an already-present label can also make parking fail before the digest is updated.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:17000-17042 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `needs_human_park_project` does not pass `--item-labeled` when the tracking issue already has `ai:needs-human`.
  WHY: The helper attempts to add the existing label, causing an API error and leaving the item labeled but absent from the digest.
- scripts/unblock_scan.py:248-251 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The parked-item skip does not check `NEEDS_HUMAN_DIGEST_ENABLED`.
  WHY: When the kill switch is false, already-parked items are still skipped before reaching the planner that restores legacy close behavior.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:477-515, 531-568 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: Parking and pruning use uncoordinated read-then-PATCH updates to the digest body, allowing concurrent writes to overwrite entries.
  WHY: A stale body snapshot can erase a newly parked entry, leaving the item labeled with its trusted verdict marker but missing from the operator-visible digest; one reviewer rated a related concurrent-park case NIT while the others rated the race MAJOR.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:349-365, 792-795 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: A failed `needs_human` operation can trigger the fallback Telegram alert as if a close had succeeded.
  WHY: The operation sets `ops_failed=true` but does not set `close_failed`, so the existing fallback guard can produce a misleading alert.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:836-837, 978-979 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The poller environments default `NEEDS_HUMAN_DIGEST_ENABLED` to true, enabling the feature by default in consumer repositories.
  WHY: A consumer repository without the `ai:operator-step` label may fail on the first park call, although the reviewer notes the feature is effectively dormant by default.
- scripts/unblock_scan.py:138-156 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_latest_verdict` uses iteration order to break ties when trusted comments have equal `created_at` timestamps.
  WHY: Same-second verdict comments can cause an older verdict to shadow the newer one and lead to an incorrect skip or extra dispatch.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Kill switch `NEEDS_HUMAN_DIGEST_ENABLED` (default `true`, defaulted inside both scripts). `false` restores today's behaviour."
  expected_change_site: scripts/unblock_scan.py ~250
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  EVIDENCE: The parked-item skip does not check the flag, so already-parked items do not reach the judge for legacy close behavior.
- requirement: "the terminal paths named in the plan (project failed after exhausted recovery or judge budgets, and the project terminal states that today wait for a person) call the same helper through the existing script path"
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh call sites for `security_pass_terminal_failure`, `security_pass_closed_fix_failure`, `security_pass_fix_reissue_exhausted`, `mark_validation_failed` (three), `finalize_integration_merge_if_needed`, the integration-conflict-capped branch, `unblock_handover_judge_output`, and the judge-cycle/recovery-exhausted paths.
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The helper invocations exist at every call site, but the `if [ "${UNBLOCK_JUDGE_ENABLED:-true}" != "false" ]` guard at lines ~17009-17012 short-circuits every terminal path to `outcome=skip detail=unblock_judge_pending` whenever the flag is true (the default). For the non-failed-project terminal states (security-pass-failed, validation-failed, final-merge-exhausted, integration-conflict-capped), the unblock judge never picks them up because they do not carry an `ai:unblock-*` block label, so the helper effectively never runs in those cases. The acceptance criterion "the helper is called from every terminal path" is met syntactically but not functionally.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/unblock_scan.py:248-251 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The parked-item skip does not check `NEEDS_HUMAN_DIGEST_ENABLED`.
  WHY: Already-parked items remain skipped when the kill switch is false, preventing the planner from restoring legacy close behavior.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:471-473, 120-128 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: `needs_human_park` adds `ai:needs-human` before finding or updating the digest, and the label-add does not allow an existing label.
  WHY: An existing label can make parking fail; if a later digest operation fails after label-add succeeds, the labeled item is skipped on subsequent scans without a digest entry.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:17012-17015 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: `needs_human_park_project` does not pass `--item-labeled`.
  WHY: The helper attempts to add an existing label and can fail without creating or updating the digest entry.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:531-538, 566-568 (needs_human_prune); 477-515 (needs_human_park) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: Concurrent pruning and parking can overwrite the digest with a stale body snapshot.
  WHY: The new entry can be lost while the item remains labeled and is skipped on later scans.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:349-365, 792-795 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: A failed `needs_human` operation can trigger the fallback Telegram alert as if a close had succeeded.
  WHY: `ops_failed=true` is set without setting `close_failed`, allowing the fallback guard to issue a misleading alert.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:836-837, 978-979 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The poller environments default `NEEDS_HUMAN_DIGEST_ENABLED` to true.
  WHY: A consumer repository without the `ai:operator-step` label may fail on the first park call, though the reviewer says the feature is effectively dormant by default.

- Requirement: "Kill switch `NEEDS_HUMAN_DIGEST_ENABLED` (default `true`, defaulted inside both scripts). `false` restores today's behaviour."
  Expected change site: scripts/unblock_scan.py ~250
  Evidence of absence: The parked-item skip does not check the flag, so already-parked items do not reach the judge for legacy close behavior.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: needs_human_park and needs_human_prune functions | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: Concurrent updates to the digest body lack atomicity.
  WHY: Concurrent park or prune operations can overwrite the body with stale content and lose entries.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:470-489 | severity=high | confidence=[5]

- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: `needs_human_park` and `needs_human_prune` PATCH paths, lines ~496-515 and ~531-568 | severity=high | confidence=[4]

  PROBLEM: Equal `created_at` timestamps are resolved by iteration order rather than numeric comment ID.
